items.title: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence
items.summary:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

(Image credit: Claudia Rosel)
items.t: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence

items.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.
items.t: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland

items.title: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
items.summary: Despite rising tension, President Trump told an Israeli outlet he may not make a decision on his next move in the Iran war until 2027.
items.t: Trump insists he's "not rushing to make any decisions on Iran"

items.title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
items.summary:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that sparked widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

Continue reading...
items.t: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid

items.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
items.summary: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.
items.t: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science

items.title: FBI criminal database hacked
items.summary: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.
items.t: FBI criminal database hacked

items.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
items.summary: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.
items.t: Man convicted of starting palisades fire

items.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
items.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.
items.t: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace

items.title: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike
items.summary: The Pentagon is preparing to release findings of its investigation into the attack that killed six U.S. soldiers in Kuwait early in the Iran war.
items.t: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike

items.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
items.summary: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020.  It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.
items.t: French police officers convicted of racist assault

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.summary:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

Continue reading...
items.t: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse

items.title: The mysterious migration of monarch butterflies
items.summary: Photographer Jaime Rojo says an iconic 1976 National Geographic cover showing monarch butterflies captivated him, inspiring his own photography. Rojo's new book "Monarchs" chronicles ways we can help save this beloved insect.
items.t: The mysterious migration of monarch butterflies

items.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
items.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.
items.t: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait

items.title: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you"
items.summary: The princess reflects on her cancer journey in the documentary and speaks to others about their experiences.
items.t: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you"

items.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
items.summary: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.
items.t: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week

items.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
items.summary: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
items.t: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal

items.title: New day of protests across France
items.summary: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.
items.t: New day of protests across France

items.title: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer
items.summary: Princess Kate made the announcement on social media after visiting the London hospital where she received treatment.
items.t: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer

items.title: How China gets access to American AI chips
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO following an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. After the Nvidia scandal, China's access to American-made technology and advanced AI chips came under renewed scrutiny. Ramy Inocencio traveled to Southeast Asia to learn more about Chinese usage of American chips.
items.t: How China gets access to American AI chips

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
items.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.
items.t: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal

items.title: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi
items.summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin appeared to make little progress in their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China.
items.t: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi

items.title: British man recalls ‘despair’ over son’s death after fall from Cyprus window
items.summary:
Joshua Foster tells of moment he ‘lost control’ of two-year-old when he fell from fourth storey of hotel

A British father who was fined by the courts after his two-year-old son fell from a fourth-floor window during a family holiday in Cyprus has recalled his “despair” when the boy slipped from his grasp.

Joshua Foster was handed a €3,000 (£2,500) penalty after he pleaded guilty to a charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act. Prosecutors in Cyprus had refused to drop the case against him.

Continue reading...
items.t: British man recalls ‘despair’ over son’s death after fall from Cyprus window

items.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.
items.t: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants

items.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
items.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.
items.t: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2

items.title: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI
items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores is allegedly the leader of a cartel responsible for drug distribution and importation.
items.t: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI

items.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
items.summary:
U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

(Image credit: Efrem Lukatsky)
items.t: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules

items.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
items.summary:
Moscow intelligence thought to be behind plan to kill musician Kyivstoner before concert in Denmark

Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper.

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark,” Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. The expulsion will happen within seven days.

Continue reading...
items.t: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged Moscow link to attempted killing of rapper

items.title: 11/21: CBS Saturday Morning
items.summary: The stock market sees its lowest week of 2026. Plus, the magical migration of monarch butterflies. All this and more.
items.t: 11/21: CBS Saturday Morning

items.title: Denmark says Russia behind plot to kill U.S.-Ukrainian citizen on its soil
items.summary: Officials said police thwarted the attempt when they arrested three men with links to the Danish criminal underworld in a car before the rapper Kyivstoner was set to perform at a concert north of Copenhagen in late September.
items.t: Denmark says Russia behind plot to kill U.S.-Ukrainian citizen on its soil

items.title: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast
items.summary: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship remains stranded off the coast of south-western France after running aground. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and potentially causing pollution. The ship was not carrying any cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter. Dan Quinlan reports.
items.t: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast

items.title: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences
items.summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk said was likely an "intentional provocation" timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer in Conflict and Security at King's College in London, Domitilla Sagramoso, shares further insights.
items.t: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences

items.title: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe
items.summary: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us the latest from Paris.
items.t: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe

items.title: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks
items.summary:
As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks.
NPR's Scott Simon talks with Phillips O'Brien of St. Andrew's University.
items.t: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks

items.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
items.summary:
A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.

(Image credit: Seth Wenig)
items.t: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI

items.title: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma
items.summary: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and the stigma surrounding menstruation. By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.
items.t: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma

items.title: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border
items.summary: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military Friday, state-affiliated media reported, amid escalating border tensions with neighboring Eritrea. France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti tells us the latest.
items.t: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border

items.title: Music strikes a chord at French protest
items.summary: Throughout history, protest songs have brought people together across genres, rallying against war, racism, inequality and the establishment. Music is also playing a key role in the youth-led demonstrations here in France. Our reporters went to meet some of the musicians using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.
items.t: Music strikes a chord at French protest

items.title: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ as UK makes deals on trade and young people
items.summary:
All options open in future talks, says Ed Miliband, while prime minister hails ‘a good day for Britain and Europe’

The UK rejoining the EU could be on the table in informal discussions between Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels, Ed Miliband has said.

The foreign secretary said “all options” would be examined in the process, after the prime minister agreed deals on trade and young people with the bloc on Friday.

Continue reading...
items.t: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ as UK strikes deals on trade and young people

items.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
items.summary:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.

Continue reading...
items.t: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs

items.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
items.summary: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.
items.t: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes

items.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.
items.t: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen

items.title: Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle
items.summary: The proposed breakthrough could reshape mathematical research, but still needs independent verification. It's the latest in a string of cases where AI has outpaced humans in solving famous maths problems.
items.t: Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle

items.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
items.summary: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.
items.t: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake

items.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
items.summary: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.
items.t: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat

items.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.
items.t: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia

items.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
items.summary:
Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”

Continue reading...
items.t: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve

items.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
items.summary: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.
items.t: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise

items.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
items.summary: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.
items.t: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway

items.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
items.summary: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.
items.t: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit

items.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
items.summary:
Efforts to establish rules for AI-powered killer robots and drones have run aground. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva ended Saturday with an agreement to extend discussions for two more years.

(Image credit: Omer Urer)
items.t: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in

items.title: Man convicted of arson over deadly 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles
items.summary: A 30-year-old man has been convicted of causing one of the most destructive wildfires in the history of Los Angeles. The verdict came after the case was retried.
items.t: Man convicted of arson over deadly 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles

items.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges
items.summary:
Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet

Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.

Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges

items.title: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars
items.summary:
Victoria police say boy, 17, communicated with offenders under username ‘Onepercent’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian police allege a 17-year-old boy tasked others to carry out a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken identity kidnapping that resulted in the partial amputation of a victim’s finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.

The boy, who was arrested on Friday afternoon, allegedly communicated with the offenders under the username “Onepercent” on the encrypted communications app Signal.

Continue reading...
items.t: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars

items.title: Brazil ex-President Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital over abdominal pain
items.summary: Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized in Brasilia with intestinal obstruction. The former far-right Brazilian leader is receiving pain medications, his son Carlos said.
items.t: Brazil ex-president Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital over abdominal pain

items.title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
items.summary:
Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last.

As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last

items.title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation
items.summary:
Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.

After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.

Continue reading...
items.t: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation

items.title: 11/20: The Takeout with Major Garrett
items.summary: Trump touts summit with Putin and Xi in first news conference since Asia trip; Poland accuses Russia of "intentional provocation" after missiles land in its territory.
items.t: 11/20: The Takeout with Major Garrett

items.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
items.summary:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Continue reading...
items.t: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ on US tech firms that build datacenters abroad

items.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
items.summary:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

  • Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Continue reading...
items.t: Global stock markets slump as Anthropic IPO fails to stem AI sell-off

items.title: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine
items.summary: On the outskirts of Kyiv, one family prepares for the fifth winter of war against Russia -- stockpiling food and fuel and trying to maintain as much a sense of normalcy as possible.
items.t: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine

items.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
items.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.
items.t: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation

items.title: Repression against Iranian lawyers increases
items.summary: At least 135 lawyers in Iran have been subjected to repressive measures over the past year. UN experts warn that this seriously jeopardizes the right of those accused to trial in a constitutional court.
items.t: Repression against Iranian lawyers increases

items.title: Russian missiles pummel Ukraine and hit NATO soil in Poland
items.summary: Missiles flew into Poland overnight as Russia hit Ukraine with "one of the largest attacks" since the war began, killing at least 8 people.
items.t: Russia missiles pummel Ukraine and hit NATO soil in Poland

items.title: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?
items.summary: The Taliban rulers in Afghanistan have accused Pakistan of aiding and sheltering armed resistance groups. The allegations come amid heightened tensions and are likely to deepen the rift between the two neighbors.
items.t: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?

items.title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results
items.summary:
At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

items.t: Trump to hold press conference after meeting with Xi and Putin

items.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
items.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.
items.t: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit

items.title: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: independents
items.summary:
The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.

This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.

items.title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
items.summary:
Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

(Image credit: Finn Gomez)
items.t: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa

items.title: U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say
items.summary: Israel wants a new joint operation with the U.S. against Iran, but it's unclear whether President Trump is willing to resume military action, and if so, to what extent.
items.t: U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say

items.title: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
items.summary:
"We're not going to shut down the war," Sen. Ron Johnson said as Republicans and Democrats struggle to reach a government funding deal.

items.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
items.summary:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike

The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”

A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Traumatizing’: hunger striker in ICE detention tells of force-feeding ordeal – and what made him crack

State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors

Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
items.t: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

items.title: Vape users hospitalised after losing consciousness, prompting public health warning in New South Wales
items.summary:
Testing confirms presence of etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials said.

NSW health on Friday issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.

items.title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
items.summary:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

Continue reading...
items.t: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers

China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

items.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.summary:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

items.t: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.summary:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Continue reading...
items.t: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

items.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
items.summary:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse

A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

items.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
items.summary:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Continue reading...
items.t: Fears grow over US sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling

items.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.summary:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Continue reading...
items.t: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
